text.p: These are the main headlines of the news reported by Radio Latvia at noon on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
- A new Reform Party may be created soon on the basis of a split-away group of the nationalist LNNK party, led by former member and leader Alexandr Kirshteins.
- Latvian newspapers are critical of the amendments in the election law, which says parties must have existed for at least three years to be able run in elections.

- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel in an interview with the International Herald Tribune said that the Madrid meeting on NATO should result in a definite statement with regard to the Baltic security.
